history.summary: A fairly-priced, highly liquid 3BR in a proven Bedok Reservoir development with verified 6.4%/yr appreciation and a 3-min walk to Bedok Reservoir MRT (DT30). The catch: the growth catalyst (DTL) is already priced in, gross yield is a mediocre ~3.2%, and the listing doesn't disclose floor/facing — the single biggest value driver in this development, where only reservoir-facing stacks above ~floor 4 get the open-water view that drives resale premiums.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $2.2M ($1,597 psf) sits exactly between the two recent same-size (1,378 sqft) comps: $2.03M/$1,473 psf for a low-floor unit in Apr-26 vs $2.37-2.40M/$1,717-1,742 psf for mid/high-floor units in Aug-Sep-25. If this is a mid/high-floor reservoir-facing unit, $2.2M is below comps and a Buy; if low-floor or non-reservoir-facing, it is ~8% above the latest identical print. Appreciation is genuinely strong and verified (6.39%/yr CAGR, 129 resale transactions, zero new-launch bias) and liquidity is excellent, but there is no remaining infrastructure catalyst (DTL opened 2017), yield is ~3.2% gross, the lease has 82 years left (~76 at a 2032 exit), and ~2,300 new D16 units (Bayshore Drive + New Upper Changi GLS) hit the market from 2026. Verify floor/facing before offering; fair value is $2.05-2.10M for low floor, $2.2M only for a high-floor reservoir view.
red_flags: Floor and facing not disclosed — in this development non-reservoir-facing units have blocked views and poorer ventilation (8 of the stacks face the water; floors 4+ clear the tree line)
Latest identical-size transaction (Apr-26, low floor) closed at $2.03M — asking is $170k (8.4%) above it

82-year remaining lease (from 2009) — ~76 years at a 2032 exit, approaching the 70-year soft floor where financing sentiment weakens
Resident-reported niggles: rush-hour traffic noise on Bedok Reservoir Rd, undersized gym (<10 machines for 561 units), facilities now 11 years old
catalysts: Verified resale momentum: project avg PSF rose from $1,229 (2021) to $1,676 (2026); May-26 prints hit $1,763-1,842 psf for mid-size units — market still firm
HDB-upgrader demand from Bedok/Tampines heartland keeps the buyer pool deep at the $2.0-2.4M 3BR quantum
Longer-term east-side uplift: Paya Lebar airbase relocation (2030s) and Bayshore transformation lift the whole D16 narrative, though neither is specific to Bedok Reservoir
Listing marked 'Negotiable' and listed only 29 May 2026 — seller anchoring high early; comp data supports negotiating toward $2.05-2.10M

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Current 3BR listings in the project ask $5,500-6,000/mo (project average ~$4.70 psf/mo). At $5,800/mo the gross yield is ~3.2% — typical for an OCR family-sized unit, not a yield play. Tenant demand is steady but local-family/regional-professional driven (reservoir lifestyle, DT30 at 270m, Temasek Poly nearby); it lacks a CBD or business-park anchor, and Bayshore's 1,280 incoming units will add east-side rental competition from ~2029-30.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: URA cache (refreshed 4 Jun 2026) shows 6.39%/yr 5-yr CAGR on 129 resale transactions — high confidence, zero new-launch bias. Momentum is decelerating but positive: +11.6% over 3yr, +4.1% over 1yr. The 1,378 sqft stack specifically went from $1.32-1.37k psf (2021-22) to $1.47-1.74k psf (2025-26). Forward expectation: 3.5-4.5%/yr is more realistic than the trailing 6.4% — the DTL re-rating is done, lease decay starts to bite past the 80-yr mark, and D16 supply arrives from 2026. Used 4.5% in my own forward view; the trailing rate flatters this property.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: 563 units, 15 storeys, 4 units/floor. Eight stacks face Bedok Reservoir; from ~floor 4 upward the view clears the tree line to open water — these are the units that command the $1.7k+ psf prints. Non-reservoir stacks face dense internal blocks: weaker views, ventilation, and resale. Ground/low floors take Bedok Reservoir Rd traffic noise on the road-facing side. Action: get the exact block/stack/floor from the agent (listing says 758 Bedok Reservoir Rd, address suggests one of the road-side blocks) before pricing the offer.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Forward-looking haircut of URA trailing 6.39%/yr CAGR (129 resale txns, ura_cache 2026-06-04): DTL catalyst fully priced, lease decay past 80yr, ~2,300-unit D16 supply from 2026

history.summary: Renovated reservoir-facing 3BR corner unit asking $1,625 psf — roughly 8-12% below the project's 2026 3BR transaction band of $1,763-1,842 psf, and below the $2.205M the same 1,292 sqft stack fetched in Aug-2024. Entry discount plus a proven 6.4%/yr URA appreciation track and deep liquidity (129 resale txns, 561 units, 270m to Bedok Reservoir DTL) make this a value buy, tempered by weak ~2.9% yield and no fresh infrastructure catalyst.
history.rating_rationale: (1) Price: $2.1M / $1,625 psf vs 2026 comps $1,763-1,842 psf for 1,216-1,259 sqft 3BRs — a ~$200K margin of safety; the identical 1,292 sqft layout sold for $2,205,000 ($1,707 psf) in Aug-2024, and project avg PSF has risen ~6.6% since 2024. (2) Unit quality: reservoir-facing corner — the 8 reservoir stacks are the prime stacks in this development — with ~$200K renovation in 'showflat condition'. (3) Fundamentals: URA 5-yr CAGR 6.4%/yr on 129 pure-resale transactions (confidence 1.0, no new-launch bias); 561 units and a $2.1M quantum sit in the liquid sweet spot. (4) Offsets: gross yield only ~2.9%, future-potential score 1/20 (DTL already priced in), 82-yr remaining lease, and the discount needs verification at viewing — a very low floor (01-05) would explain part of it, though even low-floor mid-size 3BRs printed $1,720-1,809 psf in 2025-26.

history.summary: Ground-floor 980 sqft patio 2BR at $1.58M ($1,612 psf) in a fundamentally solid development — 270m to Bedok Reservoir DTL, 561 units, 6.4%/yr URA CAGR on 129 resale transactions. But the ask prices a no-view ground unit at the PSF level high-floor 2BRs fetched in Sep-2025 ($1,618-1,646 psf), while low-floor 2BR comps printed $1,547-1,563 psf — and Waterfront Isle's entire premium is the reservoir view this unit doesn't have.
history.rating_rationale: (1) Price: low-floor 904-915 sqft 2BRs transacted $1.405-1.43M ($1,547-1,563 psf, Aug-2025/Jan-2025); applying the ~8-10% 2026 momentum seen in larger units puts fair value at ~$1.50-1.53M — the $1.58M ask is ~4-6% above, at high-floor PSF for a ground-floor unit. (2) Unit type: ~65-75 sqft of the strata area is outdoor patio (PES), priced at full PSF but worth ~half; ground floor forgoes the reservoir view that drives this project's prime-stack pricing. (3) Fundamentals are good — 6.4%/yr URA CAGR (129 resale txns, no new-launch bias), 3.3% yield on a realistic $4,300/mo rent, liquid $1.4-1.6M quantum, 270m MRT. (4) Becomes a Buy if negotiated to ~$1.50-1.52M; at ask, the entry premium eats the first year of appreciation.

history.summary: 1378sqft 3BR at $2.2M / $1596 psf, ~9% below the Waterfront Isle median of $1763, 270m from Bedok Reservoir MRT (DTL) in a well-regarded (8.9/10) reservoir-facing development. 7.36%/yr appreciation on 129 txns and reservoir views give it a real D16 story; prior call was Neutral but the current discounted entry and MRT proximity nudge it higher.
history.rating_rationale: Upgrading from the prior Neutral: at $1596 psf the unit is ~9% under its development median, sits 270m from Bedok Reservoir MRT, and carries a solid 7.36%/yr resale CAGR on 129 transactions. Aging facilities needing upgrades and the leasehold clock keep it at Buy rather than Strong Buy, but the value/location combination is genuinely attractive.

history.summary: A 1BR shoebox at Waterfront Isle (Bedok Reservoir, D16) priced at roughly fair value — the verified 12-month average is ~S$1,633 psf, so the S$1,549 ask looks cheap on a pooled basis but is essentially fair once shoebox PSF premium is accounted for.
history.rating_rationale: Verified transactions show a 12-month range of S$1,292-1,915 psf (avg ~S$1,633), and the S$1,549 psf ask sits below that average. But small 1BR units structurally command higher PSF than the pooled mix (which includes larger units like the 1,227 sqft Oct 2025 sale at S$1,915 psf), so a 581 sqft shoebox at S$1,549 psf is closer to fair value than a bargain — consistent with the algo's near-zero +0.1% cohort premium. The age-adjusted -9.5% rests on a decent 129-txn appreciation base, but the size cohort is thin (5 txns), so I discount the cohort read. RCR/D16 region carries a moderate forward prior (~+3.5%). With aging facilities noted in reviews, no dated catalyst, and only fair (not cheap) pricing, this is a Neutral — a fine hold but not an edge.

history.summary: A 1,378 sqft 3BR — the largest 3BR format at Waterfront Isle — asking $2.20M ($1,597 psf), the cheapest 3BR psf in the project's live book. The headline 7% discount to the project median is a size-mix artifact: the project's smaller 3BRs (1,163-1,259 sqft) print $1,763-1,842 psf, while this exact 1,378 sqft size has only three prints in 24 months — $1,717 psf (fl 06-10, Aug-25), $1,742 psf (fl 11-15, Sep-25) and $1,473 psf (fl 01-05, Apr-26). The ask sits almost exactly midway between the low-floor and mid-floor comp levels, and the listing discloses no floor or facing — in a development whose entire premium is the reservoir view above ~floor 4, that is the single unresolved fact that decides whether this is a 7% discount or an 8% premium.
history.rating_rationale: Priced inside its own fair-value band, not below it, once the right comp set is used. (1) The -7.2% vs project median is a size-mix artifact — the repo's own age- and size-band-adjusted comparator puts this unit at -1.1% vs D16 peers, i.e. fair. (2) Same-size evidence brackets the ask: mid/high-floor 1,378 sqft printed $2.365M-$2.40M in Aug/Sep-2025, but the only 2026 print of this size closed at $2.03M on floors 01-05 — so the ask is either ~7% cheap (mid/high floor) or ~8% dear (low floor), and the listing won't say which. This project's 1,378 sqft low-floor discount is consistent across history (-18% in 2021, -15% in 2025/26), so the floor question is worth ~$300k. (3) The 782 score leans on trailing appreciation (10.08 of 42.1 MMR points above base, from a 7.36% 5yr CAGR) which current priors give ~0 forward power; substituting the OCR realized-forward rate (3.7%/yr) drops the all-cash 7yr return from ~6.9% to ~3.7%/yr. Its dev_size/buyer_pool credit also runs on a wrong 922-unit count (the project has 561). (4) Carry is weak: 2.89% gross / 1.7% net on a well-evidenced $5,300/mo (39 URA contracts). (5) The format is the project's thinnest: 3 prints in 24 months vs 13 for the 1,100-1,300 sqft band, so exit liquidity is materially worse than the project's headline 129-transaction depth implies. Against that, the fundamentals are real — 270m to DT30 Bedok Reservoir (DTL), 561 units, deep Bedok/Tampines upgrader catchment, 82 years of lease. Fair price, unverified discount, weak carry: Neutral. Verify the floor before anything else — floor 6+ in a reservoir-facing stack at $2.20M is a Buy; floors 01-05 makes it an Avoid against its own $2.03M Apr-2026 comp.
red_flags: Floor and facing undisclosed — decisive here: 1,378 sqft on floors 01-05 has printed 15-18% below mid/high floor in this project across 2021, 2022 and 2026 (Apr-26: $2.03M / $1,473 psf). At $2.20M the ask is 8.4% above that comp.

Listed at the same $2.20M since 5 Jun 2026 (~8 weeks, relisted 21 Jul to refresh the date) while being the cheapest 3BR psf in the project — a sitting cheapest ask usually signals floor/facing/format defect rather than a bargain.
The apparent discount is a size-mix artifact: project median psf is pulled up by smaller 3BRs; against same-size, same-age peers the unit is only -1.1% (fair value, no margin of safety).
score_1000 782 is inflated for current priors — 10.08 MMR points come from a trailing 7.36% CAGR (≈0 forward power), and dev_size/buyer_pool are computed on 922 units when the project has 561.
Weak carry: 2.89% gross / 1.7% net yield on a well-evidenced $5,300/mo rent; ROI depends almost entirely on price appreciation.
Thin format cohort: only 3 prints of 1,378 sqft in 24 months (vs 13 in the 1,100-1,300 sqft band) — slow exit for the project's largest, highest-quantum 3BR.
Lease: 99 years from 26 Nov 2009, ~82 years remaining (raw_analysis overstates this as 85) — ~75 at a 7-year exit.

D16 supply at exit: Bayshore precinct GLS (~1,280 units, tender closed Jul 2026), New Upper Changi Rd GLS (~1,040), Sky Eden @ Bedok, plus the sister Waterfront Waves/Key/Gold resale book competing in the same micro-market.

Stacked Homes notes non-reservoir-facing stacks have poor outlook and ventilation, an undersized gym (<10 machines for 561 units) and a tight two-lane entrance; residents report facilities needing upgrading at 11 years old.

realsmart.sg REALSCORE unavailable — the public /p/waterfront-isle page resolved and confirmed (Waterfront Isle, D16, 561 units, 2015, 864 transactions to 7 Jul 2026) but serves the lite template with no REALSCORE, % profitable or annualized-return figures, and the /map fallback needs a logged-in session this unattended run does not have. Fields left null rather than guessed — the downside/profitability check on this project is simply not done.
catalysts: 270m (3 min) to DT30 Bedok Reservoir MRT on the Downtown Line — a genuine walk-to-MRT in a deep HDB-upgrader catchment (~1,440 Bedok flats reaching MOP/resale in 2026 feed the upgrader pool).

Bayshore precinct build-out and TEL/Sungei Bedok interchange lift the D16 narrative over a 5-7yr hold — new-launch benchmarks above $2,000 psf pull resale comparisons up (though the same GLS adds competing supply).

If verified as floor 6+ in one of the 8 reservoir-facing stacks (open water clears from ~floor 4-5 per Stacked Homes), the ask is 7-8% below the Aug/Sep-2025 same-size prints of $2.365M-$2.40M — that is a real entry discount.

Cheapest 3BR ask in the live book ($1,597 psf vs $1,625 and $1,711 for the 1,292 and 1,227 sqft listings) and unsold for 8 weeks — negotiating room toward the $2.03-2.10M same-size comp level is plausible.

Below the 3.5% comfort zone; the large 1,378 sqft 3BR does not command rent proportional to its size, so this is a capital-appreciation bet with thin carry, not a yield play.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The 7.36%/yr URA 5yr CAGR (129 txns) is real but backward-looking and partly a 2021-26 regime effect — this project's own 1,378 sqft prints went $1,321 psf (2021) to $1,742 (2025), which is the whole market's bull run, not a project edge. Current priors give trailing CAGR ~0 forward power, so I override to the OCR realized-forward rate of 3.7%/yr; on that basis the all-cash 7yr return is ~3.7%/yr rather than the ~6.9% in roi_projections. The forward case rests on region (OCR) and the Bayshore/TEL halo, not on momentum.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No profile researched for Waterfront Isle (stack_profile: not_researched), so the stack could not be joined. Public research (Stacked Homes) says 8 of the stacks face Bedok Reservoir and open water clears from roughly floor 4-5; non-facing stacks get a poor outlook and weaker ventilation. Address on the listing is 758 Bedok Reservoir Road. The project's own prints show the 1,378 sqft format splitting hard by floor tier (fl 01-05 $1,473 psf vs fl 06-15 $1,717-1,742 psf, Apr-26 vs Aug/Sep-25) — establish floor and facing at first contact; everything else about this call is secondary to it.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: OCR realized-forward baseline from the repo's 28-district panel backtest (docs/AUDIT_JUN2026.md); the 7.36% figure is a trailing resale CAGR and is de-weighted to ~0 forward power under current priors.
